subject: english
chapter_title: Two Stories about Flying: The First Flight and the Black Aeroplane

concepts.title: The Young Seagull's Fear of Flying
concepts.definition: A young seagull alone on his ledge is too afraid to fly, convinced his wings will not support him, even though his brothers and sister have already flown away the day before.
concepts.key_idea: The great expanse of sea stretched down beneath the ledge, and the fear of falling keeps the seagull rooted while hunger grows in him.
question_patterns: why was the young seagull afraid to fly
how was the young seagull different from his brothers and sister
describe the seagull's ledge above the sea
what kept the young seagull on his ledge
why did the seagull's family leave him alone
how does fear hold the young seagull back

solution_steps.explain: The young seagull stays alone on the ledge; his siblings have flown away.
He believes his wings will not carry him over the vast sea below.
The parents taunt and threaten him, hoping hunger will force him to fly.

concepts.title: Hunger as the Teacher of Flight
concepts.definition: The mother flies close with a piece of fish and stops just out of reach, and hunger overpowers fear: the seagull dives at the food and finds his wings spread and carrying him in flight.
concepts.key_idea: The seagull's first flight begins as a plunge for food and ends as triumph, with the whole family flying round him in joy.
question_patterns: how did the seagull's mother help him learn to fly
what made the young seagull take his first flight
how did hunger overcome the seagull's fear
describe the role of the piece of fish in the story
how did the family celebrate the seagull's first flight
what lesson does the seagull's first flight teach

solution_steps.explain: She flies near him with fish, tempting him and stopping just short of his beak.
Diving at the fish, the seagull instinctively spreads his wings and finds himself flying.
Hunger drives out fear, showing that necessity teaches what warnings cannot.

concepts.title: The Pilot Lost in Storm Clouds
concepts.definition: The pilot of a Dakota aeroplane flies into huge storm clouds while dreaming of breakfast in England, and inside the black clouds his compass, radio and fuel all fail him.
concepts.key_idea: The aeroplane turns and twists in the clouds, the instruments die one by one, and nothing outside the window is visible.
question_patterns: why did the pilot fly into the storm clouds
what happened to the aeroplane's instruments inside the clouds
why was the pilot dreaming of breakfast in england
describe the troubles of the dakota aeroplane in the storm
how did the compass and radio fail the pilot
what did the pilot see when he entered the clouds

solution_steps.explain: The pilot leaves Paris hoping to reach England for a big English breakfast.
He ignores the risk, flies into huge black storm clouds, and loses sight of everything.
The compass turns, the radio goes dead, and the fuel tanks are almost empty.

concepts.title: The Mysterious Black Aeroplane and the Safe Landing
concepts.definition: A strange black aeroplane appears beside the failing Dakota and guides it out of the storm, but at the landing the woman in the control centre says no other plane was seen on the radar.
concepts.key_idea: The rescuer remains unexplained, leaving a mystery about who or what guided the pilot safely through the storm.
question_patterns: who helped the pilot land safely and how
what did the woman in the control centre say
why is the black aeroplane called mysterious
how was the pilot guided out of the storm clouds
what does the ending of the black aeroplane suggest
was there really another aeroplane on the radar

solution_steps.explain: The black aeroplane signals the pilot to follow and leads him down towards safety.
The Dakota lands safely, and the pilot turns to thank the other pilot but finds no one.
The control centre woman confirms no other aeroplane appeared on radar, deepening the mystery of the helper.

questions: Why was the young seagull afraid to fly? Do you think all young birds are afraid to make their first flight?
